openings.claim: A household-surname misplacement can supply an alternate retrieval address: convert a verified mismatch into a behind-desk paper pointer from the reserved reader's surname to the book's actual divider region. This evaluates a bounded probe; the eventual pickup improvement remains unproven.
openings.delta: Divider cards narrow the expected region and the incumbent slip records temporary locations. The proposed pointer uses the adverse mismatch itself as an alternate search key. The clerk checks that candidate first and invalidates the pointer whenever moving the book. A pointer controls search order, never entitlement to receive the book.
openings.prediction: If household mismatches cause repeated searches, affected pickups will reach the correct candidate at the first indicated region, reducing second-location searches. Unrelated pickups should show no improvement. This does not establish the 95% target.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is simply re-shelving mismatches under the reserved surname. If misplacement is a one-time sorting error, re-shelving should match or outperform pointers without their lookup and maintenance cost; alternate-address conversion predicts value when household-based placement recurs.
openings.defeat: Pointers fail to reduce second-location searches for implicated holds, become stale despite clerk movement updates, or cause ambiguous candidates that cannot be resolved before handoff. Preparation exceeding ten clerk-minutes defeats fit under the original task.
openings.probe: Using existing paper and timing sheets behind the desk, the sole clerk records verified mismatches encountered during preparation, with total daily preparation capped at ten minutes. Time subsequent affected pickups and record first-location success, candidate ambiguity and pointer staleness; compare with matched pickups after ordinary re-shelving. Keep all names behind the desk and retain hold verification before every handoff. Stop the probe if verification is unavailable. Measure preparation and movement-update work separately, including their combined burden.
assumptions: The existing hold process permits unambiguous verification of the requested book and entitled reader; this capability is not supplied.
Mismatch encounters recur often enough to evaluate alternate pointers.
Pointer creation and upkeep fit the preparation allowance without impairing prompt pickups.
